title: Agarikon: A Screened Index of Psychedelic Medicine
description:
Agarikon is the reference layer for psychedelic medicine. Most information about this field lives in fragments that never connect: a clinic listed in one directory, its trials in a federal registry, the researchers in the literature, the law that permits the work in a statehouse database, the money behind it in disclosure filings. Agarikon joins those layers into one index and cites the source at every edge. This deposit is the data behind agarikon-index.com.

What it covers (this snapshot): 2,247 treatment clinics and 217 retreats or legal-access points across 75 countries; 1,600 registered clinical trials and 4,521 trial-location rows; 8,904 researchers against a 31,498-work publication corpus and its co-authorship graph; 167 organizations that fund, supply, train, insure and regulate the field; 1,534 tracked state legislative bills; and federal series covering DEA production quotas and CMS payment and claims data.

Why it can be trusted. The value of an index is not how many rows it holds but how many of them are real. Agarikon is screened, not scraped. Sources routinely present records that look in-scope and are not, and the pipeline removes them under explicit, published rules: relevance classification when data is ingested, validation when it is merged, and quarantine with a written reason before anything is published. Nothing is silently dropped; excluded records are retained with their reason so every decision is auditable. The screening record ships with this deposit as EXCLUSION_LOG.md and exclusion_log.csv, and it is a feature of the methodology rather than a footnote to it.

Provenance and licensing are mixed, and stated per source rather than blanket:

  • Clinical trials — ClinicalTrials.gov (U.S. Government, public domain)
  • CMS Open Payments, Medicare Part B, DEA quotas and Federal Register — U.S. Government, public domain
  • Publications and author metrics — OpenAlex and PubMed (CC0 or permissive)
  • State legislation — LegiScan, licensed CC BY 4.0, attribution required ("via LegiScan" plus the bill URL, shipped in the attribution column and to be preserved in any reuse)
  • Clinic and retreat listings — aggregated from public directories and state licensing feeds; these are screened aggregations rather than independently verified field data, and directory-sourced listings are not relicensed here

Scope, stated plainly. The clinics dataset is a screened directory aggregation. A legal-status classification is present on every facility row; the enabling statute is cited where one exists, which covers retreat and legal-access rows with a mappable jurisdiction and is largely absent for ordinary clinics, since those operate under generally applicable medical law rather than a psychedelic-specific statute. Trial-location rows the registry published without a facility name are flagged unnamed and are not distinct sites. The policy set is a controlled-substance corpus with a psychedelic-specific subset flagged psy, not a curated psychedelic bill tracker. exclusions.json states the anesthesia residual that remains after filtering. These are the honest edges of a living index that rebuilds daily and publishes its own change log.

Full methodology, coverage and per-source detail: agarikon-index.com/data
notes: Compilation (c) 2026 Erich Mayne / Agarikon, released CC BY 4.0. Individual records remain under their respective source licences; see the description. U.S.-government-sourced data is public domain. Rebuilt daily; each quarterly release is a frozen snapshot, and the concept DOI always resolves to the latest.
